question: Does the shipped Blob component prove a two-project Runtime+WPF source design?
conclusion: Artifact and call-chain evidence supports a native x64 module plus a managed VM SDK adapter and XML-driven common WPF configuration/display. It does not prove the original source repository/project split; a custom Blob WPF extension remains conditionally possible via an already-loaded assembly.

observed: IMVSBlobFindModu.dll is x64 PE without CLI directory.
IMVSBlobFindModuCs.dll is AnyCPU .NET Framework 4.6.1, MVID 1d550689-0379-4822-8b69-8713d2324342, refs mscorlib/VM.Core/VM.PlatformSDKCS.
Cs wrapper type IMVSBlobFindModuTool extends VM.Core.VmModule; Run calls ModuleManager.SyncSelfRun(ID); result routes through QueryModuleOneResult and SetModuleResult.
VM.Core.VmModule module creation places typeName in IMVS_SYNC_ADD_ONE_MODULE_INFO.strModuleDllName and calls SyncAddOneModule.
WPF GetExternTabWin tries loaded module+Control assembly and same-directory Control.dll, then caller falls back to ParamsTabControlBase.
Blob module directory inventory has 11 files and no IMVSBlobFindModuControl.dll.
inferred: IMVSBlobFindModu.dll is the Blob native Runtime implementation candidate based on exact module identity and SDK registration/execution path.
The normal UI likely uses common WPF metadata rendering if there is no already-loaded module-specific Control assembly.
